_comment: Proposed fixes for Hollywood: shown as the infographic timeline on hollywood/index.html.
Hand-curated. Review about once a quarter: update status, cost, and outcome, add new projects.
date      YYYY-MM-DD (or YYYY-MM-01 / YYYY-01-01 when only month or year is known)
summary   one or two plain sentences: what it is
status    Planned | In design | In progress | Completed | Revised | On hold
cost      { usd: number, label: text shown on the page }
outcome   what it does or has done, in plain words
sources   at least one { name, url }. Entries without a source are skipped.
inTotal   optional. false = cost is part of a bigger item, so it is left out of the total

items.title: Lake Drive seawall with removable panels
items.summary: A new seawall along North and South Lake Drive with 20 openings that are closed with panels before king tides.
items.outcome: With all panels in, Intracoastal water stayed off the street during the September 2026 king tide. Water can still bubble up through storm drains; one-way valves are being added.

items.title: Stormwater Master Plan
items.summary: A 20 to 30 year plan with 81 projects: pump stations, injection wells, backflow valves, higher seawalls, and raised roads.
items.outcome: Adopted June 2025. Small fixes under $4M come first from current fees; $25M to $40M projects wait for bonds and grants.

items.title: A1A drainage, pump stations, and seawall
items.summary: FDOT project on A1A by Hollywood Beach: four stormwater pump stations near Azalea Terrace, Van Buren, Sherman, and Franklin Streets, plus a seawall.
items.outcome: Under construction since June 2025, due summer 2028. Meant to stop A1A from flooding at high tide.

items.title: Tidal flooding barriers and seawalls
items.summary: Raised seawalls and tidal flood barriers on public land, paid for with state grants and the city's 2019 voter-approved bond.
items.outcome: Includes the Lake Drive panels. In 2025 the city asked the state for $10.2M more for this work.

items.title: Swale restoration pilot
items.summary: Pilot and feasibility study for restoring grassy swales citywide so rain soaks in instead of pooling on streets.
items.outcome: Half funded by a Resilient Florida grant.
